LESSON: READING SYLLABLES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.1: Reading syllables
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading syllables, part of Reading in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How do we make syllables? 2. How do we read three letter words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading syllables together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Unity is enhanced as the learner with other chant rhymes on syllables in unison.

• Integrity is developed as the learner with others practices fairness taking turns while blending sounds and reading

syllables.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Ethnic and racial relations enhanced where the learner reads sounds and forms syllables collaboratively with others across

ethnic borders.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Reading across the other Learning Areas require blending of sounds to form syllables, syllables to form words, words to form

sentences and later paragraphs. Syllables reading is necessary.
